patients.label: 33-year-old woman with a scalp nevus sebaceous harbouring an eccrine poroma and a trichoblastoma, treated by complete excision
attribution_limitations: Source conflict on the nodule count: the abstract says the long-standing plaque progressively developed into two nodular growths, while the Figure 1 caption describes a solitary nodular lesion (the case text describes one nodule). Both count statements are recorded as review_only source_conflict facts; the case-text nodule stays accepted.
The nodule is printed as 1.2 x 1 x 1 cm in the case text and as 1 × 1 × 1.2 cm in the Figure 1 caption: the same three numbers in a different order, so not recorded as a value conflict.
The case text gives the lesion site only as scalp-level within the plaque; the right parietal location is stated only in the Figure 1 caption.
The plaque colour is pink to brown in the case text and yellowish in the Figure 1 caption; descriptive wording differs and is not reconciled.
The trichoblastoma finding is described in the sentence after the plaque biopsy result ("Additionally ... was also observed") but that sentence does not name its specimen.

The text gives no order between the biopsy-based diagnosis and the complete excision (basis wording only), and the Figure 5 caption title says intraoperative and postoperative views while its lead sentence says intraoperative view.

claims.text: Skin biopsy was taken from the plaque and the nodule. The plaque showed epidermal papillomatosis with acanthosis, increased sebaceous glands and abortive hair follicles, and a basaloid follicular proliferation with peripheral palisading; the nodule showed small cuboidal basaloid cells with ductal differentiation. These findings were consistent with nevus sebaceous, trichoblastoma and eccrine poroma, diagnosed as arising within a nevus sebaceous.

evidence.quote: A skin biopsy was obtained from both the verrucous plaque and the nodular lesion.
The plaque biopsy demonstrated epidermal papillomatosis with acanthosis associated with an increase in sebaceous glands and abortive hair follicles, consistent with nevus sebaceous (Figure 2).
Additionally, a follicular proliferation composed of basaloid cells with palisading cells at the periphery was also observed, consistent with trichoblastoma (Figure 3).

The biopsy of the nodular lesion revealed a proliferation of small cuboidal basaloid cells with ductal differentiation and anastomosing bands within a fibrovascular stroma, consistent with eccrine poroma (Figures 4A, 4B).
Based on the clinical and histopathological findings, a diagnosis of eccrine poroma and trichoblastoma arising within a nevus sebaceous was established.
